population: Patients with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced NSCLC previously treated with platinum doublet & immunotherapy
outcome: ORR 43%, Median PFS 6.5 months, Median OS 12.6 months
key_finding: Confirmed clinical response in 43% of evaluable patients; secondary KRAS switch-II pocket alterations and MET bypass identified upon relapse.
claim_grounding: Among 112 evaluable patients, objective response occurred in 43% of patients, with median duration of response of 8.5 months and median progression-free survival of 6.5 months.

population: KRAS p.G12C-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer with prior systemic therapy
outcome: Confirmed ORR 37.1%, Disease Control Rate 80.6%, Median OS 12.5 months
key_finding: Significant anti-tumor activity and durable disease control; ctDNA profiling revealed polyclonal resistance mechanisms including KRAS Y96D and parallel EGFR/HER2 activations.
claim_grounding: In the CodeBreaK 100 registrational phase 2 trial, oral sotorasib (960 mg once daily) demonstrated confirmed objective response in 37.1% of patients with pretreated KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC.

population: Preclinical in vitro & in vivo patient-derived xenograft models of KRAS G12C NSCLC
intervention: Direct covalent KRAS G12C inhibitors alone or combined with SHP2/pan-ERBB inhibitors
outcome: Complete suppression of adaptive ERK rebound and prevention of emergent secondary mutations
key_finding: Acquired resistance driven by secondary KRAS mutations (Y96C, R68S) and RTK/SHP2/SOS1 feedback loops.
claim_grounding: Resistance frequently arises via secondary KRAS mutations that impair drug binding (G12D, G12V, Y96C, R68S) or through upstream RTK activation (MET, HER2) and downstream SHP2/SOS1 feedback loops.

population: 1,795 individuals with early Alzheimer's disease (MCI or mild dementia with confirmed amyloid pathology)
outcome: 27% slowing of clinical decline on CDR-SB at 18 months (P<0.001)
key_finding: Robust clearance of amyloid protofibrils and statistically significant preservation of cognitive and functional endpoints.
claim_grounding: Lecanemab reduced brain amyloid-beta burden on PET scans and led to a 27% slowing of clinical decline on the CDR-SB at 18 months compared to placebo (difference -0.45; P<0.001).

population: 1,736 early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease patients with low/medium and high tau burden
outcome: 35.1% slowing of decline on iADRS at 76 weeks in low/medium tau; complete amyloid plaque clearance in 80%
key_finding: High-rate plaque clearance allows finite-duration treatment completion; clinically meaningful slowing of disease progression.
claim_grounding: Donanemab significantly slowed clinical progression by 35.1% on the integrated Alzheimer Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) at 76 weeks in participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer disease.

population: 2,539 adults with obesity (BMI >=30 or >=27 with weight-related comorbidity) without diabetes
intervention: Tirzepatide (5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg once weekly)
outcome: Mean weight reduction of -20.9% (-23.6 kg) with 15 mg dose at week 72
key_finding: Dual GIP and GLP-1 agonism provides substantial, unprecedented weight loss and cardiometabolic improvements.
claim_grounding: Tirzepatide (dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist) at 15 mg weekly yielded mean body weight reduction of -20.9% (-23.6 kg) compared to -3.1% in the placebo group.

population: 17,604 patients >=45 years with preexisting cardiovascular disease and BMI >=27 without diabetes
outcome: 20% reduction in Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke) (HR 0.80, P<0.001)
key_finding: First evidence that pharmacotherapy for obesity reduces cardiovascular death and events in non-diabetic populations.
claim_grounding: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced the risk of primary composite endpoint (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) by 20% (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90, P<0.001).
